name: Sky-City Dwarves
background:
Sky-City Dwarves are Dwarves who have developed technology to live in airborne cities, safe from the dangers of the world below. Lightly armoured compared to other Dwarves, the Sky-City Dwarves rely on flight and ranged weapons to defeat their foes. 

The Sky-City Dwarves’ floating cities allowed them to escape the Orc armies that conquered their kin. These refugees built their small fleets into airborne cities, travelling through Tyria and surviving on trade as they slowly tried to rebuild some of what they had lost. However, when the other Dwarves were freed, the Sky-Dwarves were scorned as cowards and treated as outsiders.
backgroundFull:
The Dwarven tribes were once spread throughout Tyria, but as the plains were settled by humanity and Orcs and Giants came to the grasslands, the Dwarves retreated into the mountains. They made their homes in their mountains, creating powerful fortresses surrounded by terrace farms on the heights, and dug mines deep below. For most of their history, Dwarves had to travel overland, often through hostile territory, to visit and trade with other Dwarfholds. 

They experimented with ways to travel safely, until they discovered powered flight, and their helicopter convoys became a common sight between the mountains of Tyria. In order to facilitate this travel, large ships held aloft by lighter than air balloons were built to serve as way-stations for helicopter convoys. These were the first Sky-Ports, which offered fuel, supplies, and safety to any Dwarves who visited. 

When the Orcs conquered the mountain Dwarfholds, some Dwarves were already living and working in these early Sky-Ports. The inhabitants of these Sky-Ports were workers, traders, and engineers with little arms or equipment. Without soldiers or weapons, the Dwarves living in the Sky-Ports decided to take in what refugees they could find before fleeing from the Orc armies. 

These Dwarves discovered new resources that could be sifted from the clouds, which allowed them to remain aloft indefinitely. The sky-fairing Dwarves began to trade with others in order to get the metal, canvas, and wood they needed to maintain their ships and build new ones. Slowly, as they amassed more wealth, Sky-Ports continued to grow, until they formed self sustaining settlements called Sky-Cities. Though it took generations to become self-sustaining, the Sky-City Dwarves still remembered their conquered kin. They began to develop weapons to fight the Orcs and sought out allies to help them. 

The Sky-City Dwarves were still preparing their army when the Rift tore through Tyria. They retreated to the skies, only to discover that the Rift had damaged a number of the old Dwarfholds, and gave their kin the chance to rise up against the Orcs. They sent envoys, eager to reunite with their kin, but to their surprise, the Sky-City Dwarves were greeted with bitterness and hostility, as the other Dwarves felt that they had been abandoned. Now the Sky-City Dwarves have returned to the skies, leaving their estranged kinsfolk to rebuild the old holds, while they went back to their new way of life in the clouds. 

How will you follow the ever-shifting winds to prosperity?

specialRules.name: Buccaneer
specialRules.description: When shooting at enemies over 9" away, this model gets +1 to hit rolls.

specialRules.name: Swift
specialRules.description: This model may ignore the Slow rule.

specialRules.name: Mend
specialRules.description: Once per activation, before attacking, pick one friendly model within 3" with Tough, and remove D3 wounds from it.

specialRules.name: Spell Resistance Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 friendly units picked before the start of the game get Spell Resistance. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Counter in Melee Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 friendly units picked before the start of the game get Counter on its weapons in melee. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Rending when Shooting Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 friendly units picked before the start of the game get Rending on its weapons when shooting. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Shred in Melee Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 friendly units picked before the start of the game get Shred on its weapons in melee. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Hit & Run Shooter Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 friendly units picked before the start of the game get Hit & Run Shooter. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Versatile Reach
specialRules.description: When this unit is activated, pick one effect: until the end of the activation, all models with this rule in this unit either get +4" range when shooting or move +2" when charging.

specialRules.name: Enhanced Buccaneer Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 friendly units picked before the start of the game get Enhanced Buccaneer. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Enhanced Buccaneer
specialRules.description: If this model has Buccaneer, it always gets +1 to hit rolls from Buccaneer (instead of only when shooting over 9" away).

specialRules.name: Anti-Cover
specialRules.description: This weapon ignores Cover.

specialRules.name: Piercing Spotter
specialRules.description: Once per activation, before attacking, pick one enemy unit within 30" and in line of sight of this model and roll one die, on a 4+ place a token on it. When attacking, friendly units may remove tokens from their target before rolling to block to get +AP(X) on their weapons, where X is the number of removed tokens.

specialRules.name: Melee Slayer
specialRules.description: When charging, this model's weapons get AP(+2) if most models in the target have Tough(9) or higher.

specialRules.name: Crossing Strike
specialRules.description: Once per activation, when this model moves through enemy units, pick one of them and attack it with this weapon as if it was shooting. This weapon may only be used in this way.

specialRules.name: Destructive
specialRules.description: When attacking units with more than half of their total size or Tough value (for single-model units), those hits get AP(+1).

specialRules.name: Precision Marksman
specialRules.description: When shooting at enemies over 9" away, this model gets +1 to hit rolls.

specialRules.name: Enhanced Precision Marksman
specialRules.description: If this model has Precision Marksman, it always gets +1 to hit rolls from Precision Marksman (instead of only when shooting over 9" away).

specialRules.name: Slow
specialRules.description: Moves -2” when using Advance, and -4” when using Rush/Charge.

specialRules.name: Tough
specialRules.description: Once a model has taken as many wounds as its Tough value, it is killed (remove from play).

specialRules.name: Spell Resistance
specialRules.description: When a unit where most models have this rule takes wounds, roll one die for each. If the wound was from a spell, then it is ignored on a 2+. If the wound was not from a spell, then it is ignored on a 6+ instead.

specialRules.name: Counter
specialRules.description: May strike first with this weapon when charged, unless this unit is Fatigued.

specialRules.name: Rending
specialRules.description: Ignores Regeneration, and for each unmodified result of 6 to hit, those hits get AP(+4).

specialRules.name: Shred
specialRules.description: For each unmodified result of 1 to block hits, this weapon deals 1 extra wound.

specialRules.name: Hit & Run
specialRules.description: Once per round, this model may move by up to 3" after shooting or being in melee.

specialRules.name: Hit & Run Shooter
specialRules.description: Once per round, this model may move by up to 3" after shooting.
